about: A CORPUS, not pairs. Measures whether the detector FINDS the genuine contradictions planted in it and how many pairs it examines to do so. The pair-level eval scores the predicate; this scores PAIR SELECTION, which is what a bucketing optimisation changes.
limitations: SYNTHETIC and small (56 facts). It measures SELECTION, not predicate quality — contradiction-core.v1 does that, and a fix must not regress either.
Every genuine pair is planted cross-file, because the detector gates on that before comparing. A same-file contradiction is out of scope here and would be a different finding.
comparisons_examined is an implementation counter, not a user-visible metric. It exists so a bucketing change is measurable rather than argued.
